This project falls under the Government-endorsed PNG Electrification Partnership (PEP), through which DFAT– alongside Japan, New Zealand and the United States – is supporting PNG to meet its target of electrifying 70 percent of the country by 2030.

projects.description: Improve the resilience of food systems and social protection of refugees in Iowara will be implemented at the refugee settlement site known as Iowara in Western Province. The Iowara population comprises of approximately 3,000 refugees and a small host population. Despite the majority of refugees arriving in the 1980s, only a small number have been naturalized. The refugee community has received limited integration support and has been left behind in terms of development due to their refugee status, particularly those who with specific needs/vulnerabilities. The focus will be on improving the resilience of the food systems for the refugee community and the social protection systems for the most vulnerable groups who have been adversely impacted by consecutive crises, including climate hazards, the COVID-19 pandemic and the Ukraine crisis.

projects.description:
Support for learning continuity during COVID-19
UNESCO Office for the Pacific States in collaboration with HQ and some members of Global Coalition for Education conducted activities as response to COVID-19  by implementing the following activities: 
i.	Teachers’ use of applications to set up online classes at home presented by Lark (May 15, 2020); 
ii.	Curating and aligning open educational resources with national curriculum, focused on aligning open resources of Khan Academy with the national curriculum of the target countries by Library without borders (May 19, 2020); and 
iii.	Leveraging open-source Moodle to build national distance learning platforms by a team of facilitators from Moodle May 21, 2020). The impact of training was evaluated and the results is guiding the planning of further response. 
d.	Weekly on-line training on learning continuity on Best Practice in distance Education
e. Training by VHS for teachers and leaders  
PNG teachers and other stakeholders are among the participants in these webinars. Blended learning and Distance Learning are the most effective medium to provide a continuity of learning for students and is particularly crucial across the Pacific where isolation, natural disasters, pandemic, and limited resources all make access to quality education a challenge. Most of the activities were conducted as technical assistance to countries and the cost are estimated based on staff cost and estimated cost for collaborating partners.

The publication “Excellence in teaching: a review of professional standards for teachers in the Pacific SIDS” was launched on 5 October. PNG is one of the countries reviewed

UNESCO has secured GPE funding with other IAs on a PacREF Implementation Rolling Plan from 2022-2024. UNESCO support will focus on:
1. Support on EMIS enhancement and use of data;
2. Inclusion of non-cognitive skills in curricular and promotion of inclusive multi-sensory approach to education; 
3. Inclusive education.

framework.name: Peace
framework.description:
Harnessing the UN's reputation as an impartial steward of Bougainville peace processes, the project aims to
support leaders, parliamentarians, officials and communities in PNG, and especially the Autonomous Region in Bougainville, to further
progress ongoing post-Referendum negotiations and related peace processes at the national and regional levels and to ensure that
diverse community members' voices are included in those processes. The project will also support a number of peace-supporting
economic development initiatives aimed at increasing opportunities for women and other marginalized groups to participate in the
formal economy, targeting those communities which had been particularly affected by the consequences of the Bougainville conflict
and in alignment with the existing Bougainville innovation hubs.
